title: Field observation
description: What a trained field observer submits from the ground, before it becomes an observation. It is kept separate from `observation` on purpose: an observer reports what they saw with their own uncertainty, in the shape of the instrument they already use, and the conversion to a priceable observation is a documented step that can be re-run when the mapping improves. The shape follows the YIAGA Africa observer instrument so that an existing deployment of several thousand observers can submit without being retrained on our vocabulary.

observerOrg.description: The organisation that deployed the observer. The individual observer is never identified in a Mapomo document; the organisation holds that mapping and we do not.

observerRef.description: Opaque, org-issued code for the observer, stable enough to detect a systematically deviant reporter and meaningless outside the deploying organisation. Never a name, a phone number or a device identifier.

deployment.description: Where the observer was posted. Assignment area, not live position: an observer's real-time location is not ours to hold.

assignmentType.description: A roving observer covers ground a stationary one does not; the same count means different things.

sightings.description: What was seen during the coverage window. One entry per trace type; an entry with a count of zero is information, not an empty record, and is kept.

attribution.description: What the observer read off the material itself. An observer records the branding they saw; they do not decide who is behind it.

brandingSeen.description: The physical mark the attribution rests on.

condition.description: State of the material. A weathered poster prices differently from one put up this week, and 'removed_since' is how a takedown gets recorded.

language.description: BCP 47 tag of the message, where there is one. Language of the ground campaign is a finding in itself.

note.description: Free text from the observer, in their language. Never contains a person's name; the submission form says so and the intake check enforces it.

submission.description: How the report reached us. Rural submissions arrive late and out of order, and a pipeline that assumes otherwise silently drops the places that matter most.

instrumentVersion.description: Version of the observer form the report was filled on. Two versions of a question are two different questions.

verification.description: What the deploying organisation did with the report before it reached us. Their quality control is part of our provenance, not a black box upstream of it.

conversion.description: The link to whatever this report became. Written by the intake step, never by the observer. A report that produced no observation keeps a reason, because a systematic reason is a finding about the instrument.

mappingVersion.description: Version of the instrument-to-observation mapping used. Re-running an old report through a new mapping must be reproducible.
